title: Yankees’ Jazz Chisholm Jr. collides with Jasson Domínguez, leaves game early
content:
New York Yankees second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. collided with right fielder Jasson Domínguez — seemingly taking an elbow to the head — in the fourth inning of Monday night’s 7-3 loss to the Detroit Tigers. Chisholm fell after the collision and remained on the ground in the outfield for a while before he managed to stand up and leave the game.

Oswaldo Cabrera took over for Chisholm at second base. At the end of the game, Chisholm was still going through the concussion protocol, the Yankees said.

As Chisholm was on the ground in shallow right field, a Yankees trainer appeared to check his neck and head. He lay on his back for several minutes with manager Aaron Boone standing nearby. Chisholm eventually walked to the dugout without aid.

Domínguez made the catch, though the Yankees were trailing at the time of the apparent injury.

The collision happened as Hao-Yu Lee’s high popup drifted into shallow right field, with Chisholm and Domínguez charging it from opposite directions. Domínguez said he tried to call Chisholm off of the ball. However, Chisholm was running with his back to the infield.

“It was really unfortunate,” Domínguez said. “I mean, they were playing the infield in. So when he hit the ball, in my mind, I’ve got to go catch that ball. I called it, but obviously I didn’t call it loud enough.”

Chisholm seemed to run straight into Domínguez’s left elbow before falling to the ground. Domínguez remained in the game.

It’s been a rough couple of weeks for Chisholm, who was ejected from Sunday’s finale against the Boston Red Sox for slamming his helmet on the ground, and then declined to speak to the media after the game. Last Monday, Chisholm played an inning at second base with a lollipop in his mouth, sending fans into a frenzy on social media. The next day, Boone said that Chisholm’s lollipop antics “annoyed” him.

On June 18, Chisholm fouled a ball off his groin during a game against the Chicago White Sox and left in the middle of the at-bat.
